candidate_source_anchor.signature:
theorem fundamentalSolution_boundary_data {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    let F : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun x =>
      if n = 2 then Real.log ‖x‖ else ‖x‖ ^ ((2 : ℝ) - (n : ℝ))
    InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd F ({0}ᶜ : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) ∧
    ∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → ∀ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), ‖x‖ = R →
      F x = (if n = 2 then Real.log R else R ^ ((2 : ℝ) - (n : ℝ))) ∧
      inner ℝ (gradient F x) (R⁻¹ • x) =
        (if n = 2 then R⁻¹ else ((2 : ℝ) - (n : ℝ)) * R ^ ((1 : ℝ) - (n : ℝ)))

canonical_library_specification.signature:
theorem radial_gradient_laplacian
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    (g : ℝ → ℝ) (a x : E) (hg : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 g (‖x - a‖ ^ 2)) :
    gradient (fun z : E => g (‖z - a‖ ^ 2)) x =
      (2 * deriv g (‖x - a‖ ^ 2)) • (x - a) ∧
    Laplacian.laplacian (fun z : E => g (‖z - a‖ ^ 2)) x =
      4 * (‖x - a‖ ^ 2) * deriv (deriv g) (‖x - a‖ ^ 2) +
      2 * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) * deriv g (‖x - a‖ ^ 2)

source_omission_refinements_and_interfac.content: Show D=R^n minus{0} is open; for x in D, rho=norm(x)>0 and S=rho^2>0. Derive local C2 and actual zero coordinate Laplacian on D, then justify the exact candidate neighborhood-harmonic predicate on this open domain. No source conclusion at the excluded pole follows from arithmetic log/rpow totalization.

For n>2 put alpha=2-(n:real), q=alpha/2 and g_power(s)=s^q. At every S=norm(x)^2>0 prove local C2 of g_power, and its scalar derivatives g_prime=q*S^(q-1), g_second=q*(q-1)*S^(q-2). The scalar hypothesis of the B-node must be discharged internally.
For n=2 put g_log(s)=(1/2)log s. At S=norm(x)^2>0 prove local C2 and derivatives g_prime=1/(2S), g_second=-1/(2S^2), internally. No log smoothness premise is added to the source F signature.

On the entire punctured neighborhood prove the literal source F agrees with the relevant squared-norm composition: norm(x)^(2-n)=(norm(x)^2)^((2-n)/2), or log norm(x)=(1/2)log(norm(x)^2). Positive-base real-power and logarithm identities must be justified on an open neighborhood, not only at one evaluation point. Exponents use real subtraction.

Prove C2 of each literal F branch on D using the appropriate scalar profile and smooth squared norm, or another valid direct calculation. This is part of harmonicity to prove, not a binder. A pointwise gradient/Laplacian identity alone does not silently discharge this regularity component.

For n>2 and x!=0 derive the actual Euclidean gradient: gradient F(x)=(2-n)*norm(x)^(-n) times x. This is an unprinted required derivative result; any generic-formula specialization also must identify dim(E)=n and the literal F on the punctured neighborhood.

For n>2 and x!=0 compute the actual coordinate/Euclidean Laplacian, not an assumed harmonic predicate: Delta F=0. With q=(2-n)/2, the candidate generic expression is4*S*q*(q-1)*S^(q-2)+2*n*q*S^(q-1), whose coefficient vanishes because2*(q-1)+n=0. All derivative, real-power and dimension algebra remains unproved.
For n=2 and x!=0 derive the actual Euclidean gradient: gradient F(x)=norm(x)^(-2) times x. The raw source does not print this formula.
For n=2 and x!=0 compute the actual Laplacian: Delta F=(-2+n)/S=0 for S=norm(x)^2. This is a separate logarithmic calculation and is not the degenerate power formula obtained by setting n=2.

For every R>0 and norm(x)=R derive x!=0 and the literal F value log R for n=2 or R^(2-n) for n>2. The all-positive-R quantification is an explicit ASTIS expansion of the source reader computation: printed1.4 uses R=1 and R=epsilon in(0,1), not a separately printed all-R theorem.

Under R>0 and norm(x)=R, calculate the actual inner product of gradient F(x) with R^(-1) times x. The target is R^(-1) for n=2 and(2-n)*R^(1-n) for n>2, using inner(x,x)=R^2 and the branch gradient. This is exactly the sealed boundary pairing claim; it is not an abstract manifold-normal or Green integral statement.

For the negative radial vector derive inner(gradient F(x), -(R^(-1) times x)) = -inner(gradient F(x),R^(-1) times x). At the source inner sphere R=epsilon, this gives-(2-n)*epsilon^(1-n) in the power case or-epsilon^(-1) in the log case. The sealed F theorem itself states only the positive-vector pairing; this sign conversion remains an explicit downstream obligation.

Relate the explicit vector R^(-1)x to the actual outward unit normal of the ball/sphere and its negative to the inner outward annulus normal, with all positive-radius/smooth-boundary geometry. The scalar pairing theorem does not itself construct or verify a manifold normal, annulus smoothness, orientation convention, surface integrability or Green theorem. Those remain separate downstream obligations.

Use natural n>=2 to split exactly n=2 or n>2, proving both conditional F branches and the conjunction of harmonicity plus all positive-radius values/pairings. The else branch cannot use truncated natural subtraction; all exponents in the candidate are real. Neither branch alone proves the all-dimensional source-anchor interface.
